name: Gilgit Serena Hotel
pros: Ranked #1 of hotels in Gilgit on Tripadvisor; the only true 5-star in the city
Large landscaped garden, Rakaposhi-facing rooms and free airport shuttle
Well-trained, attentive staff and impeccable cleanliness (Booking.com 8.8/10 over 178 reviews, with 9.1 cleanliness)
cons: Easily the most expensive option in town
Restaurant menu selection is fairly limited
take: The default safe choice for foreign and business travelers who want secure, comfortable, internationally-run lodging. You pay a premium, but nothing else in Gilgit matches it.

name: Madina Hotel 2
pros: Booking.com 8.6/10 over ~109 reviews; rooms set around a peaceful garden courtyard
Two-minute walk from the airport, ~10 minutes to the bazaar
Owner Mr. Yaqoob is a long-standing local fixer who helps arrange treks and transport
cons: A backpacker/traveler hub rather than a polished hotel
Rooms are simple; don't expect luxury finishes
take: Gilgit's classic traveler base camp: clean, friendly, great value and a good place to meet other trekkers and sort onward logistics.

name: Grand Continental Hotel
pros: Strong Google score (4.0 over 257 reviews) for a mid-range property
On Riverview Road in Chinar Bagh, near the Gilgit River
Free breakfast, WiFi and parking
cons: Listed as a B&B/inn tier, not a full-service hotel
take: A reliable, well-reviewed mid-range pick in the leafy Chinar Bagh riverside area, good if you want decent comfort without Serena pricing.

name: PTDC Gilgit Motel
pros: One of the oldest established hotels in Gilgit, centrally located near the river
Big lawn/garden and well-regarded restaurant with good dinner and breakfast service
Garden-view rooms are notably nicer than the standards
cons: State-run upkeep is inconsistent; some rooms and bathrooms feel dated
take: A dependable, centrally-located government-run motel with a pleasant lawn and good food. Ask specifically for a garden-view room, as quality varies.

name: Riveria Hotel
pros: Excellent flower-filled garden and a restaurant well known locally for its food
Sits right by the Gilgit River with rooftop terrace and garden views
Friendly, helpful staff and genuinely cheap rates
cons: Mixed cleanliness reports: dusty, musty rooms noted by some guests
Hot water only available on demand roughly 7-10 am; limited heating
take: A cheap, characterful riverside spot loved for its garden and food, but a budget stay with hit-or-miss housekeeping. Best in warmer months.

name: Marco Polo Hotel
pros: Very cheap, around PKR 3,500/night
Central at Yadgah Chowk, Khomer, close to bazaar amenities
Rooms include TV, room service, heater/geyser and 24-hour security
cons: Only ~15 rooms, so it books out fast in peak season
Basic standard-hotel finishes; no notable views
take: A no-frills, budget-friendly base in central Gilgit. Fine for a functional, cheap night near the bazaar if you book ahead.

name: North Inn Hotel
pros: Long-running property established in 1987 at Khomer Chowk
Central location convenient to the bazaar and transport
cons: An older, basic property; expect dated rooms
Little verifiable recent review data online
take: A veteran budget inn in central Gilgit. Worth considering as a fallback when the better-reviewed budget options are full, but inspect the room first.
